endorsements.quote: Explanation strategies should be adapted to different user groups, from clinicians to patients to engineers.
Involvement of a more diverse and representative group of stakeholders can ensure that domain weighting better reflects end users’ needs and expectations.

unlisted_practices: Embed trust-oriented safeguards procedurally across the entire AI lifecycle, from design to deployment, rather than assessing trustworthiness only post hoc.
Use a structured trustworthy-AI framework such as ALTAI as a starting scaffold and adapt it to the project context.
Systematically integrate societal, labor, and democratic impact considerations into oversight structures, stakeholder engagement, and long-term governance even when developers deprioritize them.
Align AI development workflows with adaptive governance structures able to incorporate feedback, absorb policy shifts, and maintain ethical continuity over time.
Use co-creation workshops with diverse stakeholders to define performance thresholds, context-specific harms, and explanation strategies.
Follow privacy-by-design principles in system architecture.
Adopt ALTAI-like processes early in system design to prepare for conformity assessments under the EU AI Act.

screen.reason: This is a Viewpoint / case study describing how a governance framework (ALTAI) can be applied in clinical AI projects, accompanied by a small internal survey of project developers.
